displayName: Web route handler → Spring Boot 3 REST service (controller · service · JdbcTemplate repository)
description: The pattern for a routine that answers HTTP requests and reads or writes a database — a PHP controller method, a front-controller action, a script behind a URL. It becomes a real Spring Boot 3.2 service on Java 21: a @RestController that keeps every method, path, status code and body shape the signed spec's http_contracts state (errors through a @RestControllerAdvice that reproduces the legacy 404 / 422 / 400 bodies instead of Spring's ProblemDetail defaults), a @Service holding the business rules and the order of checks, and a @Repository on JdbcTemplate with every value bound as a parameter (never concatenated, even where the source concatenated it), one method per data_accesses claim, with @Transactional where statements must commit together. Bean validation carries the legacy rules and messages. The tests are the contract: @WebMvcTest MockMvc tests assert each response a caller can get, @JdbcTest tests run the repository against an embedded H2 database built from schema.sql, and plain unit tests pin the rules. Builds and tests OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (spring-boot-starter web, jdbc, validation, test and H2 are baked into its cache). The reference resource is an invoice API; a routine is migrated by renaming the resource and substituting its own routes, rules, statements and tables.

matches.fallback: Used for routines that serve HTTP routes and read or write a database (a spec with http_contracts and data_accesses). Other PHP routines with no web surface still use the narrower archetypes that match them by name.
